name: Chris Bumstead
who: Five-time Classic Physique Mr. Olympia champion, retired from competition in 2024.
why: Defined the modern classic physique look and built a business empire (RAW Nutrition, Bum Energy, CBum Fitness) that outgrew the sport itself.

name: Sam Sulek
who: College-age gym creator turned the biggest name in raw workout-vlog content since 2023.
why: Set off a wave of copycat long-form training vlogs; his views routinely outstrip his subscriber count.

name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
who: Seven-time Mr. Olympia, actor, former California governor, still runs the Arnold Sports Festival and a daily fitness newsletter.
why: Amplifier: fitness is a fraction of his output, but his Pump Club newsletter and Arnold Classic events move the whole industry when he speaks.

name: David Laid
who: Natural-aesthetics creator who went viral as a teenager for a dramatic physique transformation.
why: One of the longest-running faces of the 'aesthetic natural' training niche, still posting after nearly a decade.

name: Lexx Little
who: Powerlifter and bodybuilder with dwarfism who competes and trains alongside able-bodied lifters.
why: Built one of fitness's most inspirational niches by posting real training numbers, not just transformation photos.

name: Larry Wheels
who: Powerlifter, strongman, and arm-wrestler who documents extreme-strength feats and PED-assisted training openly.
why: Bridges powerlifting, strongman, and bodybuilding audiences with genuine elite-level lifting numbers.

name: Eddie Hall
who: 2017 World's Strongest Man and former deadlift world record holder (500kg raw).
why: Crossed strongman into mainstream media via a Netflix documentary and a headline boxing match against Hafthor Bjornsson.

name: Hafthor Bjornsson
who: 2018 World's Strongest Man, former deadlift world record holder, and Game of Thrones' 'The Mountain'.
why: One of the few strength athletes with genuine Hollywood crossover, plus a headline pivot into pro boxing.

name: Tren Twins
who: Identical twins Christian and Michael Gaiera, comedic gym-vlog duo who blew up in under two years.
why: Their deadpan, self-aware 'gym bro' format got copied across the creator economy faster than almost anyone else's.

name: Bradley Martyn
who: Gym-culture veteran and owner of the Zoo Culture gym chain in California.
why: One of the longest-running gym-vlog creators; turned his following into an actual gym business, not just content.

name: Mike O'Hearn
who: Veteran natural bodybuilder, model, and actor known as 'The Maniac' or 'The Titan'.
why: Over 30 years of visible relevance across bodybuilding, TV, and film work, longer than almost anyone in the segment.

name: Noel Deyzel
who: South African-born giant-frame creator known for size-focused training content.
why: Rapid follower growth on sheer physical novelty, part of the current wave of size-first, competition-optional creators.

name: Joey Swoll
who: Former gym manager turned viral 'gym positivity' creator who calls out bullying and gym-shaming clips.
why: Started an entire anti-gym-shaming content genre now copied by dozens of smaller creators.

name: Alex Eubank
who: Aesthetics-focused creator known for full-day-of-eating and cutting/bulking vlogs.
why: Popularized the modern 'lean bulk' aesthetic content format now standard across natural bodybuilding YouTube.

name: Jesse James West
who: Comedic gym-collaboration creator who films workouts with other influencers and pro athletes.
why: Pioneered the collab-heavy comedic gym-vlog format that many mid-tier creators now run on.

name: Will Tennyson
who: Scottish-Canadian fitness YouTuber known for 'try the diet of X celebrity' and coaching content.
why: A steady, credentialed voice in natural bodybuilding YouTube with almost a decade of consistent output.

name: Greg Doucette
who: IFBB pro bodybuilder and coach known for calling out fraud and misinformation in bodybuilding media.
why: A rare credentialed insider voice who publicly polices claims made by other bodybuilding influencers.

name: Derek (More Plates More Dates)
who: Researcher-creator focused on PED harm reduction, hormone science, and bodybuilding history.
why: Shaped mainstream harm-reduction discourse around PED use and co-founded a real hormone-testing business.

name: Urs Kalecinski
who: 2023 Classic Physique Mr. Olympia champion from Germany.
why: The rising European face of classic physique now that Bumstead has stepped back from competing.

name: Ramon Dino (Ramon Rocha Queiroz)
who: First Brazilian man to win a Mr. Olympia title, taking the 2025 Classic Physique crown.
why: Brought huge Brazilian and Latin American audiences into competitive bodybuilding's spotlight.

name: Nick Walker
who: Men's Open pro bodybuilder known as 'The Mutant', multiple Arnold Classic winner.
why: One of the biggest mass-monster physiques currently competing, influential in the current Open bodybuilding trend.

name: Jay Cutler
who: Four-time Mr. Olympia (2006, 2007, 2009, 2010), now runs a large supplement brand and gyms.
why: One of the sport's most successful post-competition business builders, still a reference name for casual fans.

name: Dorian Yates
who: Six-time Mr. Olympia (1992-1997), credited with starting bodybuilding's 'mass monster' era.
why: His high-intensity training template still shapes how top-level bodybuilders train decades later.

name: Regan Grimes
who: Canadian Men's Open pro bodybuilder, repeat top-5 Olympia finisher.
why: A consistent top-tier competitor representing Canada on the Olympia stage.

name: Ronnie Coleman
who: Eight-time Mr. Olympia (1998-2005), widely regarded as one of the greatest bodybuilders ever.
why: His 'Yeah buddy, lightweight' persona and record-setting Olympia run still define the sport's golden era in pop culture.
